title: Frontend Engineer (m/f/x)
description: <p>At go-e, we have been pursuing the development of our vision with passion and strength from the very beginning. We are moving in an area that is characterized by breakthroughs and growth and that requires a lot of personal responsibility and creative solution finding. On our journey towards the energy transition, the mixture of innovation and security, regional and international, self-realization and professionalism is the ideal fuel for our mutual growth.</p> <p>Help build the Portal, a modern web platform for fleet managers and technicians. As a<strong> Frontend Engineer (m/f/x)</strong>, you will turn product ideas into responsive, accessible interfaces using <strong>React and TypeScript.</strong> Join a collaborative team that values autonomy, ownership, code quality, and learning, and deliver features with visible customer impact.</p> <p>With your contribution, you will impact how people will charge their cars in the future. Come and join the team in Berlin (GER) that is building the future of innovative charger solutions for e-mobility!</p> <h3>Your area of responsibility</h3> <ul> <li>Build and deliver frontend features for the Portal using React and TypeScript.</li> <li>Work with product, design, and backend specialists to translate requirements into user interfaces.</li> <li>Integrate RESTful APIs and WebSocket communication, including asynchronous data, caching, and error handling.</li> <li>Write clean, maintainable, performant code and unit and integration tests.</li> <li>Contribute to code reviews, design discussions, and frontend architectural decisions.</li> <li>Troubleshoot existing features, improve performance, and share knowledge with other engineers.</li> </ul> <h3>Who we’re looking for<strong>:</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Strong experience building web applications with React and TypeScript.</li> <li>Experience with server-side rendering frameworks such as Next.js.</li> <li>Proficiency with modern frontend tooling and state management, such as Redux or React Context.</li> <li>Solid knowledge of HTML5, CSS3, CSS-in-JS or styled-components, and responsive or adaptive design.</li> <li>Familiarity with UI component libraries, design systems, and accessibility best practices.</li> <li>Experience with frontend build tools such as Webpack, Vite, or Babel, including bundler optimization.</li> <li>Ability to integrate APIs and WebSocket communication and manage asynchronous data flows, errors, and caching.</li> <li>An independent approach, ownership of your work, and clear communication with product, design, and engineering colleagues.</li> </ul> <h3>Even better would be</h3> <ul> <li>Experience writing developer tools, internal packages, or SDKs.</li> <li>Contributions to open-source projects.</li> <li>Experience in startup or fast-paced environments.</li> <li>Deeper familiarity with real-time or WebSocket architectures.</li> <li>(Not a must) Proficiency in one or more backend languages / frameworks (e.g. Node.js / Express / NestJS / TypeScript, or similar)</li> </ul> <h3>What we offer</h3> <ul> <li>Be one of the key drivers of our core technologies</li> <li>A high degree of freedom in the execution of your projects</li> <li>Flexible working hours</li> <li>Mental well-being support via nilo.health</li> <li>Employee discounts on our products</li> <li>Corporate discounts on a variety of brands</li> </ul> <h5><strong>About go-e</strong><br>We are a fast-growing, successful company in the field of e-mobility and have developed from a start-up to an internationally recognized player. From our headquarters in Carinthia, Austria, we have already expanded to around 20 European countries. With bold ideas based on our passion for innovative e-mobility solutions, we are already establishing future technologies today.</h5> Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

raw.title: Principal AI Engineer (x/f/m)
raw.description:
We are looking for a Principal AI Engineer to join the Practice Efficiency team at Doctolib.

Your mission will be to define and deliver how AI transforms the daily work of healthcare professionals — through intelligent scheduling, automated document processing, smart task management, and AI-assisted patient communication. As a Principal-level individual contributor, you will own the deepest technical challenges within the Practice Efficiency scope: setting the AI architecture bar, driving rigorous evaluation standards, and directly shaping how AI-powered features reach healthcare professionals and their patients at scale — starting with the Phone Assistant, currently one of Doctolib's most strategic product bets.

Working in the tech team at Doctolib means building innovative products and features to improve the daily lives of care teams and patients.

What you'll do

Your responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Own end-to-end AI architecture decisions for Practice Efficiency — from model selection and agentic system design to production deployment patterns,, and strategic build vs. buy calls

  • Architect and deliver agentic applications at scale, defining how Practice Efficiency AI features are structured, evaluated, and iterated on in production

  • Design robust, scalable AI infrastructure: model and prompt versioning, guardrails, uncertainty quantification, cost optimisation, and observability — enabling the team to ship reliably and fast

  • Lead the technical delivery of the Phone Assistant's AI capabilities, balancing ambitious product ambitions with engineering rigour and production reliability

  • Ensure responsible AI delivery in a regulated healthcare context, embedding explainability, GDPR/HDS compliance, and human-in-the-loop design across all Practice Efficiency AI features

  • Partner closely with Product Managers and cross-functional stakeholders to translate customer and business needs into sound technical decisions, acting as a bridge between engineering depth and product delivery

Who you are

Before you read on: if you don't have the exact profile described below, but you feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply.

You'll be a great fit if you:

  • Have 10+ years of software engineering experience, with at least 5 years focused on building AI products — including experience building AI systems before the rise of large language models, giving you strong fundamentals in evaluation, data pipelines, and system design under uncertainty

  • Have a strong background in building and operating large-scale distributed systems — we value deep systems engineering expertise and will consider profiles who bring exceptional scale experience alongside a solid grounding in AI

  • Have hands-on experience designing and shipping agentic applications, with a clear understanding of the challenges around reliability, observability, and evaluation in production agentic systems

  • Are product-centric by nature: you have worked closely with Product Managers and product organisations, bring genuine business sense and customer closeness, and see yourself as part of the product delivery chain — not just the technical one

  • Are fluent in English

It would be fantastic if you:

  • Have experience with LLM fine-tuning, RAG systems, or automatic speech recognition in production environments

  • Have built AI products in healthcare, financial services, or another regulated domain where safety and auditability are non-negotiable

  • Have contributed to or built shared AI platforms used by multiple product teams

Life at Doctolib Tech

  • Our solutions are built on a single fully cloud-native platform that supports web and mobile app interfaces, multiple languages, and is adapted to country and healthcare specialty requirements.

  • Our stack in this product area is Ruby on Rails and TypeScript/React in the monolith, Kotlin for new services, with Postgres, Redis and Kafka underneath.

  • We leverage AI ethically across our products to empower patients and health professionals. Discover our AI vision here.

Want to learn more about our tech culture and environment? Visit the Doctolib Tech site.

What we offer

  • A Deutschlandticket (Germany-wide public transport pass) fully paid for by Doctolib

  • 28 vacation days + 1 additional day for each full calendar year of employment (up to a maximum of 30 days)

  • Work from abroad for up to 10 days per year thanks to our flexibility days policy

  • Company health insurance with great supplementary benefits through our partner Allianz

  • Company pension scheme (bAV) through Allianz with an employer subsidy of 40% (15% within the probationary period)

  • The Doctolib Parent Care program, which includes one month additional parental leave and much more

  • Enrollment in Doctolib's long-term employee value sharing plan called DoctoGrowth

  • Free mental health and coaching services through our partner Moka.care

  • Subsidized sports membership through our partner Urban Sports Club

  • A flexible workplace policy offering both hybrid and office-based mode

  • Alongside healthy snacks and our regular breakfast buffet, we provide a subsidized meal benefit

  • For caregivers and workers with disabilities, a package including an adaptation of the remote policy, extra days off for medical reasons, and psychological support

  • Relocation support in case of international mobility

  • Access to the best AI tools for coding, development and dedicated training

Our interview process

  • Recruiter Interview

  • System Design Interview

  • Behavioral Interview

  • Engineering Manager Case

  • At least one reference check

We want your experience to be clear, respectful, and transparent. Learn more about our hiring process on our candidate experience page.

Job details

  • Permanent position

  • Ruby on Rails, TypeScript, Kotlin

  • Full-time

  • Location: Berlin

  • Hybrid work setup (up to 2 remote days per week)

  • Start date: as soon as possible

We welcome everyone

At Doctolib, we are committed to improving access to healthcare for everyone. This translates into our recruitment process. We evaluate candidates based solely on qualifications and motivation, without any form of discrimination.

The more diverse ideas are heard, the more our product will truly improve healthcare for all. You are welcome to apply to Doctolib, regardless of your gender, religion, age, sexual orientation, ethnicity, or disability.

To ensure equal opportunities, we invite you to exclude personal information (e.g., pictures, age) from your applications. If you require any accommodation, please let us know for support during the hiring process.

Join us in building the healthcare we all dream of!

Your data privacy

All information provided is processed by Doctolib for application management. For data processing details, click here: Germany | France | Italy | Netherlands. Please contact hr.dataprivacy(at)doctolib.com for inquiries or to exercise your rights.

title: IT Support Spezialist - Telematikinfrastruktur & Healthcare IT/APIs(x/f/m)
description: Gemeinsam gestalten wir die Gesundheitsversorgung der Zukunft Du hast ein starkes technisches Wissen und Lust, Dich tief in die deutsche Healthcare-IT einzuarbeiten? Dann bist Du hier richtig. Im Technical Services arbeitest Du an der Schnittstelle zwischen unserer Doctolib-Plattform und der deutschen Healthcare-IT-Landschaft. Du löst komplexe Integrationsprobleme, unterstützt unsere Kund:innen bei technischen Herausforderungen und trägst aktiv dazu bei, dass Doctolib reibungslos in die Infrastruktur unserer Kund:innen integriert ist. Du musst nicht vom ersten Tag an alles wissen. Mit Deinen fundierten Grundlagen und Deiner Motivation, unterstützen wir Dich, Dich in Themen wie die Telematikinfrastruktur und API/Konnektoren, einzuarbeiten. Deine Aufgaben Du bist technische Ansprechperson rund um die Deutsche Telematikinfrastruktur – von der Schnittstellen-Architektur über Kartenverwaltung bis hin zu Gematik-Standards. Kein Tag ist wie der andere. Produkte, die laufen: Du supportest Doctolib-Lösungen rund um die Deutsche Telematikinfrastruktur. und sorgst dafür, dass sie korrekt konfiguriert sind – und wenn doch mal etwas hakt, findest du heraus, warum. Komplexe Probleme, echte Lösungen: Interoperabilitätsprobleme mit Konnektoren und APIs gehören zu deinem Alltag – du arbeitest eng mit IT-Service-Partnern zusammen und bringst auch schwierige Fälle zum Abschluss. Tiefer tauchen, sauber dokumentieren: Du analysierst technische Herausforderungen eigenständig, hältst alles strukturiert in Jira fest und arbeitest direkt mit den Entwicklerteams zusammen, um Fehler nachhaltig zu beheben. KI als Werkzeug, nicht als Buzzword: Du nutzt KI-Tools aktiv, um schneller zu Lösungen zu kommen und Dir fundiertes Wissen aufzubauen – effizient und zielgerichtet. Wissen, das bleibt: Du teilst dein Know-how proaktiv mit internen Teams, damit Probleme gar nicht erst entstehen und unsere Kund:innen das bestmögliche Erlebnis haben. Dein Profil Das solltest du mitbringen: API-Integration und Troubleshooting sind für dich kein Neuland – du hast echte Erfahrung damit, Probleme zu identifizieren und zu lösen. Du kennst dich mit komplexen IT-Infrastrukturen, Netzwerken und sicherheitskritischen Systemen aus – und weißt, worauf es in solchen Umgebungen ankommt. Du kannst technische Sachverhalte so erklären, dass sie ankommen – egal ob du gerade mit einer Entwicklerin oder einer Praxismanagerin sprichst. Deutsch fließend (C1) und Englisch solide (B2) – du bewegst dich in beiden Sprachen sicher. Das ist ein Plus – oder du lernst es bei uns: Kenntnisse rund um die Telematikinfrastruktur, Gematik-Standards oder andere Healthcare-IT-Systeme – wer schon mal mit KIM+, eAU- oder E-Rezept-Workflows gearbeitet hat, ist klar im Vorteil. Erfahrung mit Observability-Tools wie Kibana, Datadog oder Elasticsearch. Ein Abschluss in Informatik, Medizinischer Informatik oder eine vergleichbare Berufserfahrung ist willkommen – aber kein Pflichtfeld. Was wir Dir bieten Ein von Doctolib gesponsertes Deutschlandticket, wenn Du aus dem Büro oder im Hybridmodus arbeitest Eine betriebliche Krankenversicherung mit tollen Zusatzleistungen 28 Urlaubstage + 1 Tag zusätzlich für jedes volle Beschäftigungs-Kalenderjahr (max. 30 Tage) Die Möglichkeit, bis zu 10 Tage im Jahr aus dem Ausland zu arbeiten Eine betriebliche Altersvorsorge (bAV) mit einem Arbeitgeberzuschuss von 40 % (15 % während der Probezeit) Teilnahme an Doctolibs langfristigem Mitarbeiterbeteiligungsprogramm DoctoGrowth Das Doctolib Parent Care Programm, das einen Monat Elternzeit extra u.v.m. enthält Kostenlose Mental Health- und Coaching-Sessions über einen externen Partner Zusätzlich zu gesunden Snacks und einem regelmäßigen Frühstücksbuffet, bieten wir Essensgutscheine Ein gefördertes Sportangebot mit unserem Partner Urban Sports Club Für pflegende Betreuungspersonen und Beschäftigte mit Behinderungen gibt es ein Angebot, das flexiblere Arbeitszeiten, zusätzliche Freistellung aus medizinischen Gründen und psychologische Unterstützung beinhaltet Der Interviewprozess Erstes Gespräch mit Talent Acquisition Technical Assessment Technical Interview, Assessment Review & Meet the Team Finales Interview Mindestens eine Referenzprüfung Job Details Festanstellung Vollzeit Berlin Startdatum ab sofort Hybrid erlaubt (2 Tage Homeoffice / Woche) Wir verfolgen die Vision, die Gesundheit aller zu verbessern. Dies spiegelt sich auch im Recruiting wider. Wir evaluieren Bewerbungen ausschließlich auf der Grundlage von Qualifikation und Motivation. Diskriminierung wird bei uns nicht toleriert. Je diverser unser Team und die Ideen sind, desto mehr wird unser Produkt die Gesundheit unserer Nutzer:innen verbessern können. Deshalb laden wir Dich ein, Dich bei uns zu bewerben, unabhängig von Geschlecht, Religion, Alter, sexueller Orientierung, ethnischer Herkunft oder Behinderung. Um Chancengleichheit zu gewährleisten, kannst Du in Deiner Bewerbung auf Angaben wie Fotos, Alter, etc. verzichten. Lass uns bitte wissen, welche Vorkehrungen wir treffen können, um Dich bestmöglich zu unterstützen. Wir freuen uns, mit Dir das Gesundheitswesen zu digitalisieren! Alle bereitgestellten Informationen werden von Doctolib für das Bewerbungsmanagement verarbeitet. Für Details zur Datenverarbeitung klicke bitte hier . Bei Fragen oder wenn Du Deine Rechte wahrnehmen möchtest, wende Dich bitte an hr.dataprivacy(at)doctolib.com. #LI-MZ1 Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

description: <div class="content-intro"><h4><strong>Help make the world more hospitable </strong></h4> <p>The hospitality industry is uniquely human, and it deserves technology that’s just as inspiring as the people behind it. At Mews, we’re transforming the industry with a platform that helps hotels run smarter, move faster and create better guest experiences.</p> <p>You’ll work with smart, curious people who care deeply about what they do. You’ll have autonomy and the trust to make good decisions and move quickly. And you’ll enjoy a real sense of purpose as you see the impact of what we’re building.</p> <p>If you’re motivated by ownership, curiosity and meaningful impact, and are driven to deliver consistent high performance, you’ll feel at home here.</p> <h4><strong>About the role</strong></h4> <p>Let's get into the specifics. It’s impossible to capture every nuance of a role – especially at a rapidly growing company like Mews – but if we had to distil it into a job description (which we do because this is a job description), it would be this:</p></div><p>You would own Mews' relationships with the press, turning company news, product launches and leadership insight into credible coverage across hospitality, travel, technology and business media. This is a new role, the first dedicated media relations seat at Mews, so the contacts you build and the way you work will set the standard for how we deal with the press. Hospitality technology offers good stories and unusual data to pitch, and leaders here respond to press requests within about a day.</p> <p>You would join the Communications team within Marketing and work closely with the communications lead, the colleagues who shape our stories, and leadership, product marketing and regional marketing. Day to day you would pitch journalists directly, host press briefings, handle inbound enquiries and prepare leaders to speak well in front of the press. The role is remote first in Europe, ideally near London, Berlin or Paris where many of the journalists we work with are based, with about 10% travel to meet press and attend events such as Unfold.</p> <p>Journalists respond to people they know and trust, not to mass pitches, and the strongest coverage comes from a specialist who holds those relationships personally. Mews has strong stories and data to offer, and this role exists so that someone owns that conversation: choosing the right journalist for each story, answering inbound questions quickly and accurately, and knowing when to escalate something sensitive. Done well, it builds the company's reputation with the people who cover our industry over the long term.</p> <h4>What you would do</h4> <ul> <li>Build and maintain direct relationships with journalists across hospitality, travel, technology and business media: develop stories with the communications team, pitch them proactively by phone and email, host press briefings and invite journalists to events such as Unfold.</li> <li>Respond to inbound press enquiries (currently two to three a week and growing) quickly and accurately, and escalate anything potentially sensitive to the communications lead straight away.</li> <li>Brief and coach executive and local spokespeople, and share what you learn from journalists with leadership.</li> <li>Redesign how media monitoring, journalist research and coverage reporting work using AI, and set the workflows up so the rest of the team can use them.</li> <li>Own and improve the team's media management tool, and check every AI-assisted pitch, briefing or summary before it reaches a journalist.</li> </ul> <p><strong>AI Fluency Level 3:</strong> in this role that means you have gone well beyond using AI to draft copy. You have redesigned parts of how media relations work gets done, such as monitoring, journalist research or coverage reporting, you have built approaches that colleagues now follow, and you actively question and check what AI gives you, including target lists, summaries and quotes, before anything reaches a journalist or a spokesperson.</p> <p><em>For more information on AI fluency at Mews, please refer to <a href="https://mews.atlassian.net/wiki/x/XQOskg">AI Fluency at Mews: A Comprehensive Guide for Candidates</a> on Confluence.</em></p> <h4>What you would bring</h4> <ul> <li>Seven to ten years in PR and communications with depth in B2B media relations, including time in a PR agency.</li> <li>Your own journalist contacts and hands-on experience pitching by phone, email and in person, with fully fluent English, written and spoken.</li> <li>A record of handling reactive and sensitive press enquiries under time pressure, with clear habits about when to escalate.</li> <li>Confidence preparing senior and non-expert spokespeople for press conversations.</li> <li>AI Fluency Level 3 or the equivalent hands-on experience, shown through tools or workflows you have built for media relations work, not only content you have written with AI.</li> </ul> <h4>Nice to have</h4> <ul> <li>French or German alongside fluent English, or existing relationships with journalists in the UK, France, Germany or the US.</li> <li>Experience with B2B technology clients or in hospitality.</li> <li>Experience measuring coverage and coordinating local expertise in markets where you have fewer contacts.</li> </ul><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="title">Germany</div><div class="pay-range"><span>€71.500</span><span class="divider">&mdash;</span><span>€93.000 EUR</span></div></div></div><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>Pay Transparency at Mews</strong></h4> <p>Salary ranges are provided in good faith title: Customer Success Manager, Mid Market
description: Why Harvey At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come. This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched. Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you. At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started. Role Overview As a Mid-Market Customer Success Manager at Harvey, you are the custodian of value for a portfolio of law firms and in-house legal teams across DACH — you own their mutual success plan and their renewal. You connect Harvey's technology and expertise to each customer's goals, moving them along the AI maturity curve so adoption keeps deepening, and you are directly accountable for retaining and growing that relationship. You will run your book as a portfolio, deliver a consistently high-quality customer journey at scale, and partner with Account Executives, Legal Engineers and Product to turn adoption into measurable value and expansion. What You’ll Do Deliver the customer journey : run kickoffs, implementation reviews and QBRs tailored to each customer, anchored on a mutual success plan that ties Harvey to their objectives, priorities and measures of success. Drive adoption and value : engage end users, administrators and senior stakeholders — managing partners, general counsel, heads of innovation — to position Harvey as essential to how their legal work gets done, build on proven use cases, and quantify ROI in business terms. raw.title: Langfuse - Product Designer
raw.description:
Why Design at Langfuse

Your work will shape how engineers build with AI.

Langfuse is often the primary interface engineers use to debug, evaluate, and improve their LLM applications. The designs you ship will be used for hours each day by thousands of developers and non-developers. They'll tell you about it in GitHub issues, on X, and in our community Slack channels. Everything we build is open source (MIT-licensed) and immediately visible.

The design challenges here are genuinely hard. You're designing for technical users and business users alike who care about information density, speed, and precision. Traces contain dozens of nested LLM calls with massive prompts and completions. Users need to set up evaluators, manage prompt versions, configure integrations, and build monitoring dashboards before they even start analyzing results. You need to make both the setup and the daily use feel intuitive and easy.

You will also have direct exposure to how cutting-edge LLM applications are built. Deeply understanding the problems our users solve will make you a better designer and along the way makes you an expert on LLM engineering yourself.

You will grow at Langfuse by

  • Owning our product design end-to-end. You'll be the first dedicated designer at Langfuse. Today, our engineers design as they build, which has gotten us far, but we need someone who can elevate the entire experience. You'll own the design system, and visual language across the product. You'll set the standard for how Langfuse looks and feels.

  • Making data-dense interfaces intuitive. Langfuse surfaces traces, scores, costs, latencies, token counts, prompt versions, and evaluation results. You'll figure out how to present complex, nested data in ways that help engineers find what they need fast.

  • Simplifying complex workflows. Our users run evaluations across datasets, compare experiment results, manage prompt versions, and set up monitoring. You'll map these workflows, identify friction, and design flows that feel obvious in hindsight.

  • Collaborating directly with product engineers. You'll pair with engineers, whiteboard solutions together, and ship designs that work within our existing component system (shadcn/ui, Tailwind). You'll create reusable, consistent UI patterns that the whole team can build with.

  • Shipping design straight to code. You'll use AI coding tools to implement smaller design fixes, build components for the design system, and polish UI details yourself. We are not looking for a perfect engineer here but for someone who can help themselvesherself.

What we're looking for

  • Experience in designing complex web applications, incl. a portfolio showcasing product work that users loved

  • Take ownership of our UI/UX made for developers

  • You want to talk to users

  • Hard worker and thrive working in a small and accountable team

  • Good understanding of best in class UI/UX

  • Excited about open source software and dev tools

Bonus points:

  • You can ship frontend code (we use Next.js, Tailwind, shadcn/ui)

  • ML/AI experience or familiarity with the LLM tooling ecosystem

  • Former founder or early startup experience

  • Contributions to open source projects or design systems

  • Side projects that show craft and taste

No candidate checks all boxes. If you feel you are a good fit for this role, please go ahead and apply.

Perks

  • Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

  • Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

  • Equity in the company - Every new eligible team member who joins our company receives equity.

  • Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

  • A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

  • Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here. Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

About the Role As an AI R&D Engineer in Model Training (f/m/d), you will join our model training team in Heidelberg or Berlin. Most of the team is based in Heidelberg. The model training team is building and improving our model training pipeline, which has been used to train Kolibri. You will work across our full stack. Some weeks you might be optimizing how training loads are scheduled on our cluster and making the pipeline more robust and performant so we can iterate faster. Engine Behind 120M Processed Auctions Daily The Ad Network team builds and operates the backend services that power adjoe Ads' programmatic advertising engine. description: Camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration , enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes. We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team. Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies , We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading. About the Role: Hi there! We're hiring a German-speaking ADR I to join our Account Development team at Camunda. We're a tight-knit, energetic team that takes outbound seriously without taking ourselves too seriously. We run structured prospecting motions, share what's working in real time, celebrate the wins together, and still allow for flexibility in the way we operate because booking a good meeting takes real work and progressing an opportunity puts ADRs at the forefront of a great GTM motion. This is a strong entry point into tech sales for someone who wants to learn and refine the fundamentals of prospecting, discovery, and pipeline generation inside an enterprise software motion. You'll work directly with Account Executives but will also be responsible for prospecting into your own patch. We ask that all of our ADRs have a remote environment that is conducive to consistent weekly motions and to be able to travel 4-6 times per year, usually a week or less at a time. What you will do: As an ADR I, you'll run long-term outbound and timely inbound prospecting motions to generate qualified pipeline for our sales team. Working emails, sales cadences, social outreach and most importantly calls to get in front of the right people at the right accounts at the right time. This role exists because a sustainable pipeline is built through persistence, consistency, a growth mindset and an ability to diagnose challenges and bring solutions within your own prospecting motion. Generate qualified pipeline by running outbound prospecting across email, phone, event outreach and attendance and LinkedIn into target accounts. Qualify inbound interest through ADR-led scheduled calls and convert into booked meetings for Account Executives. Research accounts, personas and signals to tailor and leverage AI for high touch low impact motions. Partner with Account Executives to understand what constitutes a quality meeting, contact and account, and adjust your approach based on feedback. Exhibit excellent operational hygiene by tracking activity and pipeline health in Salesforce and other sales tools to monitor your own inputs and performance. Learn Camunda's product and value propositions and the process orchestration space well enough to have credible, useful conversations with prospects in specific verticals. What you bring: Fluency in German Some experience with outbound prospecting or customer-facing communication is preferred. This doesn't have to be in sales. Internships, retail, hospitality, or customer support all count if you know how to build rapport with people, manage expectations and handle rejection. Comfort with strict time management and prioritization of requests. You'll be conducting a lot of calls and emails, and you're motivated by the math of it. You will also be given regular enablement and will be responsible for monitoring multiple sources of leads. Curiosity about technology and a willingness to learn a technical product. You don't need an engineering background, but you need to be genuinely interested in understanding what Camunda does and why it matters to the people you're calling. You share successes. Resilience and self-awareness. You know how to keep going without getting discouraged, and you can tell the difference between a bad day and a bad approach. Coachability. You take feedback from your manager and AEs seriously and change your approach in a timely and meaningful way based on it. Cross-functional relationships. You have a curiosity as to how things work and which individuals you can support and thus that can support you. You ask questions and challenge the status quo if you’ve experienced a better solution. Ability and/or willingness to use our product . This role is an existing vacancy #LI-JS1 #LI-Remote #DACH What We Have to Offer: Compensation We offer competitive, fair, and transparent compensation. Salary ranges are location-based, with Standard and Major markets (global tech hubs) reflecting local competition. The Annual Total Target Cash (base salary + 100% variable target, where applicable) shown below spans from the minimum in a Standard market to the maximum in a Major market. Final offers depend on skills , experience , and location , and we typically hire in the first half of the range to allow room for growth: Germany: €58,800.00 to €120,500.00 United States: $91,000.00 to $181,700.00 United Kingdom: £57,200.00 to £116,400.00 Singapore: S$113,100.00 to S$209,900.00 If you’re based elsewhere, you’ll be hired via Remote.com (our global employer partner), and your Talent Acquisition Partner will provide a personalized Total Rewards Calculator after your first interview. Equity: We also offer equity (where applicable) through our Virtual Stock Option Plan (VSOP) . Benefits & Perks We invest in your wellbeing, growth, and ability to connect, along with perks that support you no matter where you’re based. Our benefits are globally designed and locally delivered where applicable. About the Role:

Hi there! We're hiring a German-speaking ADR I to join our Account Development team at Camunda.

 

We're a tight-knit, energetic team that takes outbound seriously without taking ourselves too seriously. We run structured prospecting motions, share what's working in real time, celebrate the wins together, and still allow for flexibility in the way we operate because booking a good meeting takes real work and progressing an opportunity puts ADRs at the forefront of a great GTM motion.

 

This is a strong entry point into tech sales for someone who wants to learn and refine the fundamentals of prospecting, discovery, and pipeline generation inside an enterprise software motion. You'll work directly with Account Executives but will also be responsible for prospecting into your own patch. We ask that all of our ADRs have a remote environment that is conducive to consistent weekly motions and to be able to travel 4-6 times per year, usually a week or less at a time.

What you will do:

As an ADR I, you'll run long-term outbound and timely inbound prospecting motions to generate qualified pipeline for our sales team. Working emails, sales cadences, social outreach and most importantly calls to get in front of the right people at the right accounts at the right time. This role exists because a sustainable pipeline is built through persistence, consistency, a growth mindset and an ability to diagnose challenges and bring solutions within your own prospecting motion.

  • Generate qualified pipeline by running outbound prospecting across email, phone, event outreach and attendance and LinkedIn into target accounts.

  • Qualify inbound interest through ADR-led scheduled calls and convert into booked meetings for Account Executives.

  • Research accounts, personas and signals to tailor and leverage AI for high touch low impact motions.

  • Partner with Account Executives to understand what constitutes a quality meeting, contact and account, and adjust your approach based on feedback.

  • Exhibit excellent operational hygiene by tracking activity and pipeline health in Salesforce and other sales tools to monitor your own inputs and performance.

  • Learn Camunda's product and value propositions and the process orchestration space well enough to have credible, useful conversations with prospects in specific verticals.

What you bring:

  • Fluency in German

  • Some experience with outbound prospecting or customer-facing communication is preferred. This doesn't have to be in sales. Internships, retail, hospitality, or customer support all count if you know how to build rapport with people, manage expectations and handle rejection.

  • Comfort with strict time management and prioritization of requests. You'll be conducting a lot of calls and emails, and you're motivated by the math of it. You will also be given regular enablement and will be responsible for monitoring multiple sources of leads.

  • Curiosity about technology and a willingness to learn a technical product. You don't need an engineering background, but you need to be genuinely interested in understanding what Camunda does and why it matters to the people you're calling. You share successes.

  • Resilience and self-awareness. You know how to keep going without getting discouraged, and you can tell the difference between a bad day and a bad approach.

  • Coachability. You take feedback from your manager and AEs seriously and change your approach in a timely and meaningful way based on it.

  • Cross-functional relationships. You have a curiosity as to how things work and which individuals you can support and thus that can support you. You ask questions and challenge the status quo if you’ve experienced a better solution.

  • Ability and/or willingness to use our product.

About the Role:

Hi there! We're hiring a Senior Product Marketing Manager to join our Product Marketing team.

We're a group that cares about getting the story right, not just getting it out the door. We work closely with product, sales, and demand gen, and we hold ourselves to a high bar because our work directly shapes how the market understands what we build.

This role gives you real ownership. You'll shape positioning and messaging for a meaningful piece of our product portfolio, build the competitive intelligence that keeps our field teams sharp, and work directly with sales leaders who depend on your materials to close deals. It's a role with visible impact, not one where your work disappears into a shared drive.

As a Senior Product Marketing Manager, you'll drive go-to-market strategy for your area, from positioning through launch through enablement, while partnering with product and sales to make sure the message actually lands. This role matters because clear, credible product marketing is what turns a strong platform into a business result. Camunda operates in a technical, complex space, and getting that translation right is not optional.

What You Will Do

  • Own positioning and messaging for your product area, translating technical capability into a clear value proposition for both technical and business buyers.

  • Build and maintain a competitive intelligence program that sales actually uses, not just battlecards that sit in a folder.

  • Lead go-to-market execution for launches in your area, coordinating across product, sales, and demand gen so the message is consistent everywhere it shows up.

  • Arm the field with content that works in real conversations: pitch decks, demos, solution briefs, and objection handling.

  • Use market and customer research to inform product and positioning decisions, not just to validate ones already made.

  • Mentor and support other marketers on your team, sharing what you've learned without being asked.

What You Will Bring to the Role

  • Significant experience in B2B product marketing, ideally in enterprise software, with a track record of owning positioning and messaging end to end, not just contributing pieces of it.

  • A real competitive intelligence practice under your belt. You've built and maintained a program that sales relied on, not just responded to research requests as they came in.

  • Comfort marketing technical products to technical buyers. You can go deep enough into a technical concept to be credible with a developer, and simplify it enough to be clear to an executive.

  • Field enablement experience at scale. You've built programs that changed how a sales team talked about a product, and you know how to tell if it worked.

  • Strong cross-functional instincts. You know how to build trust with product and sales without relying on authority, and how to bring people along on a positioning decision rather than just announcing it.

  • Comfort using AI tools in your day to day work. This isn't a checkbox, it's part of how the role actually operates.

title: Regional Sales Manager, DACH (m/w/d)
description: Regional Sales Manager, DACH (m/w/d) Regional Role · Remote, based in the DACH region · Reports to: Sales Director About Everfield Everfield acquires and builds vertical SaaS businesses across Europe. Our portfolio spans more than 40 companies serving niche markets where software is mission-critical. We take a long-term ownership approach: we buy, invest, and build. We don't flip. Seven companies are in DACH, and we expect continuous growth in portfolio size and performance across all regions. We are building a small, high-impact HQ revenue team responsible for lifting the commercial capability of our portfolio companies: setting standards, identifying risk, and accelerating performance. The role reports to Everfield's Sales Director, who owns consistency of the revenue system across all regions, and works day to day with the region's General Director and the CEOs of its Business Units. The Opportunity The Regional Sales Manager (RSM) is a cluster-level revenue operator responsible for improving sales execution and accelerating organic revenue growth across a group of portfolio companies. The role partners directly with CEOs and Business Unit leaders to strengthen pipeline discipline, improve forecast accuracy, and raise commercial maturity across the region. This is not purely an advisory role. Alongside the regional remit, the RSM is expected to take direct sales management responsibility inside Business Units where that is the fastest route to growth, giving smaller commercial teams access to experienced sales leadership they would not otherwise have. As the region scales, the ambition is that one person can hold the sales management role on behalf of several Business Units at once, applying a standard across all of them. Success is reflected in improved revenue predictability, stronger pipeline discipline, and sustained bookings growth across Business Units. How the Role Operates • Two levels, one standard. The regional remit is constant: diagnostics, pipeline discipline, forecast integrity, and commercial governance across every Business Unit in the cluster. Beyond it, the role flexes. In some Business Units you will coach and support an existing sales manager. In others you will hold the sales management role yourself. • Direct team leadership where it is needed. Where you act as sales manager, you own the team, the pipeline, the forecast, and the number, in the same way a local sales manager would, and you report into that Business Unit's CEO for delivery while remaining accountable to Everfield for how the work is done. • You are not a seller. You do not carry a personal quota and you are not measured on deals you close yourself. You are measured on what the teams you lead and support deliver. • Reporting. You report to Everfield's Sales Director for standards, priorities, and development. The role is a shared resource for the region rather than a function serving any single Business Unit, acting in close partnership with Group Directors, CEOs, and sales teams. What You Will Do Sales Execution & Commercial Acceleration • Drive new and expansion bookings growth across the cluster, with consistent attention to prospecting, opportunity development, and account growth. • Act as sales manager for one or more Business Units: run the weekly rhythm, set priorities, coach the team, and hold sellers to their number. • Reduce volatility in bookings performance and increase revenue consistency across the cluster. • Strengthen proactive sales behaviour across outbound, account expansion, renewals and opportunity reactivation. • Improve sales execution across the full funnel, from lead generation through to closing and account retention. • Embed sales methodology and qualification standards, and hold teams to them through evidence rather than instruction. • Lead deal/pipeline reviews and targeted coaching to improve win rates, shorten cycle times, and build seller capability. Pipeline Discipline & Forecast Integrity • Improve forecast reliability across Business Units, working toward 5% variance or better. • Define and apply opportunity qualification standards and run structured pipeline reviews. • Ensure pipeline visibility reflects realistic execution capacity, and raise revenue risks early to Business Units and Everfield leadership, always paired with a recommended course of action rather than an open flag. • Monitor sustained underperformance patterns and ensure corrective action plans are implemented in time to matter. raw.title: Regional Sales Manager, DACH (m/w/d)
raw.description:
Regional Sales Manager, DACH (m/w/d)

Regional Role · Remote, based in the DACH region · Reports to: Sales Director

About Everfield

Everfield acquires and builds vertical SaaS businesses across Europe. Our portfolio spans more than 40 companies serving niche markets where software is mission-critical. We take a long-term ownership approach: we buy, invest, and build. We don't flip. Seven companies are in DACH, and we expect continuous growth in portfolio size and performance across all regions.

We are building a small, high-impact HQ revenue team responsible for lifting the commercial capability of our portfolio companies: setting standards, identifying risk, and accelerating performance. The role reports to Everfield's Sales Director, who owns consistency of the revenue system across all regions, and works day to day with the region's General Director and the CEOs of its Business Units.

The Opportunity

The Regional Sales Manager (RSM) is a cluster-level revenue operator responsible for improving sales execution and accelerating organic revenue growth across a group of portfolio companies. The role partners directly with CEOs and Business Unit leaders to strengthen pipeline discipline, improve forecast accuracy, and raise commercial maturity across the region.

This is not purely an advisory role. Alongside the regional remit, the RSM is expected to take direct sales management responsibility inside Business Units where that is the fastest route to growth, giving smaller commercial teams access to experienced sales leadership they would not otherwise have. As the region scales, the ambition is that one person can hold the sales management role on behalf of several Business Units at once, applying a standard across all of them.

Success is reflected in improved revenue predictability, stronger pipeline discipline, and sustained bookings growth across Business Units.

How the Role Operates

• Two levels, one standard. The regional remit is constant: diagnostics, pipeline discipline, forecast integrity, and commercial governance across every Business Unit in the cluster. Beyond it, the role flexes. In some Business Units you will coach and support an existing sales manager. In others you will hold the sales management role yourself.

• Direct team leadership where it is needed. Where you act as sales manager, you own the team, the pipeline, the forecast, and the number, in the same way a local sales manager would, and you report into that Business Unit's CEO for delivery while remaining accountable to Everfield for how the work is done.

• You are not a seller. You do not carry a personal quota and you are not measured on deals you close yourself. You are measured on what the teams you lead and support deliver.

• Reporting. You report to Everfield's Sales Director for standards, priorities, and development. The role is a shared resource for the region rather than a function serving any single Business Unit, acting in close partnership with Group Directors, CEOs, and sales teams.

What You Will Do

Sales Execution & Commercial Acceleration

• Drive new and expansion bookings growth across the cluster, with consistent attention to prospecting, opportunity development, and account growth.

• Act as sales manager for one or more Business Units: run the weekly rhythm, set priorities, coach the team, and hold sellers to their number.

• Reduce volatility in bookings performance and increase revenue consistency across the cluster.

• Strengthen proactive sales behaviour across outbound, account expansion, renewals and opportunity reactivation.

• Improve sales execution across the full funnel, from lead generation through to closing and account retention.

• Embed sales methodology and qualification standards, and hold teams to them through evidence rather than instruction.

• Lead deal/pipeline reviews and targeted coaching to improve win rates, shorten cycle times, and build seller capability.

Pipeline Discipline & Forecast Integrity

• Improve forecast reliability across Business Units, working toward 5% variance or better.

• Define and apply opportunity qualification standards and run structured pipeline reviews.

• Ensure pipeline visibility reflects realistic execution capacity, and raise revenue risks early to Business Units and Everfield leadership, always paired with a recommended course of action rather than an open flag.

• Monitor sustained underperformance patterns and ensure corrective action plans are implemented in time to matter.

Revenue Standards & Definitions

• Act as guardian of Everfield's revenue definitions in the region: what counts as a booking, how new name is separated from back to base, how recurring value is recognised, and what enters the pipeline in the first place.

• Hold those definitions consistently, including where a Business Unit's own commercial logic pushes against them, and fix the incentive, target, or CRM design underneath rather than bending the measurement.

• Make the cluster comparable to every other region, so performance can be read the same way across the portfolio.

Commercial Governance

• Ensure transparency in quota design, attainment measurement, and sales capacity planning.

• Support commission structure alignment with business goals.

• Contribute to annual, quarterly, and monthly commercial planning by reality-checking growth assumptions against pipeline health, execution capacity, and historical feasibility.

Commercial Diagnostics

• Diagnose revenue performance across segments, teams, and funnel stages, identifying where revenue is generated, stalled, or lost.

• Produce a written diagnostic and prioritised action plan for each Business Unit you take on, naming the problem, the cause, the cost of inaction, the action, the owner, and the date.

• Prioritise your own time across the cluster on distance to target, materiality to the region, and whether a documented plan already exists.

• Provide feedback on pricing discipline, discounting practices, packaging effectiveness, and ICP conversion efficiency.

• Translate performance signals into executive-level recommendations and commercial action plans.

CEO & General Director Partnership

• Act as strategic commercial partner to CEOs and Business Unit leaders, representing Everfield's revenue expectations and performance discipline.

• Challenge growth assumptions constructively and escalate persistent underperformance when required.

What Success Looks Like

In the first 12 months:

• Full visibility into the commercial funnel, aligned with HQ reporting standards.

• Acceleration of organic recurring revenue growth across the region.

• Improved reliability of pipeline data and forecast accuracy.

• Sales pipelines that more accurately predict bookings performance.

• At least one Business Unit where you hold sales management directly and the team delivers against its number.

• Reliable visibility of quota attainment and seller productivity.

• Deal reviews embedded across portfolio sales teams, resulting in higher win rates and shorter sales cycles.

• Revenue per seller increasing steadily across the cluster.

• A documented, reusable set of playbooks and diagnostics that other regions can apply without starting again.

What We Are Looking For

• 6-10 years total experience in B2B SaaS revenue roles, with at least 3-4 years in a sales management position, accountable for a team's bookings performance and not only for personal pipeline contribution.

• Track record of consistent revenue target attainment in a management role. You have owned a number and delivered against it, not only improved process quality.

• Direct experience leading and developing a sales team, including hiring, coaching, and managing underperformance. You will do this again here, inside our Business Units.

• Track record of implementing structured pipeline management: defining stage criteria, enforcing qualification standards, running deal reviews, and improving forecast reliability.

• Experience diagnosing revenue performance across the full funnel: understanding where deals are lost, why cycles extend, and what structural issues limit growth.

• Manages through CRM data: uses pipeline data to run structured deal reviews, identify risk, and hold sellers accountable to data quality. Familiar with Salesforce or HubSpot as a management tool.

• Experience working with senior stakeholders (CEOs, founders, or general managers) on commercial performance, including navigating organisational resistance and earning trust before driving change.

• Experience adapting sales management approach across companies at different sales maturity levels: able to calibrate coaching, process rigour, and expectations to fit the context.

• German fluency required, with professional English for work across the group. European B2B SaaS market experience required.

• Commercial finance literacy is a strong advantage: reading a P&L, understanding revenue recognition, and being able to argue the return on a commercial investment.

• Private-equity-backed or multi-entity SaaS environment experience is a strong advantage.

Skills

• Structured coaching and seller development: designing and running structured 1:1s, deal reviews, and field accompaniment to build individual seller capability, not just inspect opportunities.

• Pipeline discipline and forecasting: reading a pipeline critically, identifying risk early, and improving forecast reliability.

• Change management: driving commercial process adoption across multiple teams, and building momentum without relying on formal authority.

• Documentation and knowledge scale: writing down what you diagnose and what you implement, in a form another person can pick up and run. Work that lives only in conversation does not scale across a portfolio, and anything you build for one Business Unit should be reusable in the next.

• Commercial planning and challenge: building a bottom-up view of what revenue targets are achievable, pressure-testing top-down assumptions, and presenting credible alternatives to leadership.

• Commercial storytelling: presenting clear, honest risk assessments to CEOs and senior leadership, and leading a review that drives decisions rather than just restating numbers.

  • Full Business proficiency in German and English is a must

Who You Are

• You lead teams and you influence without authority. You will manage sellers directly in some Business Units and hold no formal authority in others. Both need to work. You build trust quickly and drive change through credibility, clarity, and structured analysis.

• You are hands-on with sales execution. You are comfortable stepping into real deals, reviewing opportunities with sellers, and diagnosing pipeline issues directly with the team, without needing to be the person closing.

• You combine analytical thinking with practical commercial judgement. You interpret pipeline data, and you also understand the realities of getting deals done.

• You communicate clearly and directly. You raise commercial risks early, with a recommendation attached, and challenge assumptions constructively, including when performance doesn't meet expectations.

You are pragmatic in complex environments. Portfolio companies vary in maturity and commercial model. You bring discipline without imposing rigid process that doesn't fit the situation

TA screen (30min)

Hiring Manager interview (90min)

Group Director interview

title: Member of Technical Staff - Safety
description: About Black Forest Labs We're the team behind Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX—foundational technologies that changed how the world creates images and video. We're creating the generative models that power how people make images and video—tools used by millions of creators, developers, and businesses worldwide. Our FLUX models are among the most advanced in the world, and we're just getting started. Headquartered in Freiburg, Germany with a growing presence in San Francisco, we're scaling fast while staying true to what makes us different: research excellence, open science, and building technology that expands human creativity. Why this role FLUX models ship as open weights, which gives anyone full access to the model. Our safety efforts focus on suppressing harmful behaviors and mitigating the risk of misuse, so safety has to be built into the models themselves, not bolted on afterwards. As a Member of Technical Staff on our safety research team, you'll research and ship methods that make FLUX models safe by design: from what goes into the training data to how the models are mid- and post-trained, across images, video and the text that conditions them. This is a role with real ownership: you won't just do research on model safety, you'll shape it. The methods you build ship in FLUX models with over 75 million downloads on Hugging Face and in production at some of the largest platforms in the world. What you'll work on Develop mid- and post-training safety methods for FLUX models, such as safety SFT, preference optimization and RL with safety rewards, and concept erasure. Build safety data filtering that runs at pretraining scale: classifiers and pipelines that screen billions of images, video clips and captions, with measured Pareto frontiers and precision/recall trade-offs. Make safety hold up for open-weight releases, including robustness to adversarial prompts and to downstream fine-tuning. Extend safety to the text side of the stack: prompts, captions and the text encoders that condition our models. Design evaluations and red-teaming that measure harmful generations alongside image quality and prompt following, so safety gains don't come at the cost of performance. Work directly with pretraining and post-training teams so your methods land in the release model, and publish where it makes sense. What we're looking for Hands-on research experience in visual safety: safety of text-to-image, text-to-video or vision-language models, such as harm classifiers, safe generation methods or safety benchmarks. Proven experience in at least one of: Large-scale safety data filtering: building and running classifiers or filtering pipelines over hundreds of millions of samples or more. Safety mid- or post-training: safety SFT, DPO or RL with safety objectives, or unlearning applied to large generative models. Deep familiarity with concept erasure methods (e.g. ESD, UCE, adversarial unlearning) and their failure modes, such as concept recovery and collateral damage to unrelated concepts. Track record of shipping: top-venue publications (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV) paired with production impact, or unambiguous production wins at a frontier lab. Experience with distributed training at multi-node scale. Strong PyTorch fluency; you write research code that others can build on. You work fluently with coding agents to move faster, and have the depth to verify their output and own the result. Experience running multi-agent workflows: you know which tasks to hand off and which to keep yourself, and you use the speed-up to raise the quality bar, not lower it. We'd be especially excited if you: Know how to keep safety intact after release, when others fine-tune open weights. Have tackled safety for video generation, where harm can emerge across frames rather than in any single frame. Bring experience with audio safety, especially for jointly generated audio and video, where each modality can amplify harm in the other. Have unlearned concepts from text encoders or built safety-tuned encoders (e.g. Safe-CLIP-style approaches). Have worked on text safety: LLM safety tuning, prompt and jailbreak defenses, or text safety classifiers, ideally across languages. Have applied latent-space safety methods, such as activation steering or safe guidance. Have built VLM-based safety judges or guard models for filtering or evaluation. How we work together We're a distributed team with real offices that people actually use. You'll join us in Freiburg at least 2 days a week (or one full week every other week). We'll cover reasonable travel costs to make this possible. We think in-person time matters, and we've structured things to make it accessible to all. We'll discuss what this will look like for the role during our interview process. Everything we do is grounded in four values: Obsessed. We are a frontier research lab. The science has to be right, the understanding deep, the product beautiful. Low Ego. The work speaks. The best idea wins, no matter who said it. Credit is shared. Nobody is above any task. Bold. We take the ambitious bet. We ship, we do not wait for conditions to be perfect. Kind. People over politics. We treat each other with genuine warmth. Agency without empathy creates chaos. If this sounds like work you'd enjoy, we'd love to hear from you. Compensation EUR 160K-220K + equity, depending on profile Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

  • Develop mid- and post-training safety methods for FLUX models, such as safety SFT, preference optimization and RL with safety rewards, and concept erasure.

  • Build safety data filtering that runs at pretraining scale: classifiers and pipelines that screen billions of images, video clips and captions, with measured Pareto frontiers and precision/recall trade-offs.

  • Extend safety to the text side of the stack: prompts, captions and the text encoders that condition our models.

  • Design evaluations and red-teaming that measure harmful generations alongside image quality and prompt following, so safety gains don't come at the cost of performance.

  • Work directly with pretraining and post-training teams so your methods land in the release model, and publish where it makes sense.

What we're looking for

  • Hands-on research experience in visual safety: safety of text-to-image, text-to-video or vision-language models, such as harm classifiers, safe generation methods or safety benchmarks.

  • Proven experience in at least one of:

    • Large-scale safety data filtering: building and running classifiers or filtering pipelines over hundreds of millions of samples or more.

    • Safety mid- or post-training: safety SFT, DPO or RL with safety objectives, or unlearning applied to large generative models.

  • Deep familiarity with concept erasure methods (e.g. ESD, UCE, adversarial unlearning) and their failure modes, such as concept recovery and collateral damage to unrelated concepts.

  • Track record of shipping: top-venue publications (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV) paired with production impact, or unambiguous production wins at a frontier lab.

  • Experience with distributed training at multi-node scale.

  • Strong PyTorch fluency; you write research code that others can build on. You work fluently with coding agents to move faster, and have the depth to verify their output and own the result.

  • Bold. We take the ambitious bet. We ship, we do not wait for conditions to be perfect.

title: Robotics Application Engineer
description: At Rhoda AI, we’re building the next generation of generalist intelligent robots. We own the full robotics stack from high-performance hardware and robot systems to the infrastructure and state-of-the-art foundation world models that control our robots. Our robots are designed to be generalists capable of operating in complex, real-world environments and handling long-tail edge cases, made possible by our cutting edge research and end-to-end system design. We've raised over $450M and are investing aggressively in model research, infrastructure, hardware development, and manufacturing scale-up to make generalist robotics a reality. Robotics Application Engineer – Rhoda AI GmbH (Germany) About Rhoda AI GmbH Rhoda AI GmbH is Rhoda AI's first international entity, established to own strategic partner relationships across Europe and drive deployment of Robotics as a Service (RaaS). It's a small, high-ownership team: you'll work with the Managing Director and Commercial Lead as peers from day one, with a direct line to our engineering organization in Silicon Valley. About the Application Engineering Team Application Engineering is where Rhoda's AI meets the real world. We work directly with customers and strategic partners to understand their operational problems, determine where our platform can deliver value, and lead the application of Rhoda's AI model end to end — from model post-training and data collection, to robot tooling and work-cell design, to production deployments on the customer's floor. The team sits at the intersection of engineering, product, deployment operations, and business, with members in the US and Germany. Application Engineering is organized into three complementary roles — Application Engineers, Solution Engineers, and Technical Program Managers. The Role As a Robotics Application Engineer, you are a core member of Rhoda AI's European team and the hands-on technical lead in the early stages of a partner engagement — Scoping, Proof of Principle (POP), and Proof of Concept (POC) — through to RaaS deployment. You'll determine whether a use case is feasible, design and prototype the end effectors and task tooling a robot needs to do the job, write the data collection procedures that feed our models, and post-train Rhoda's AI model to perform the task. You'll spend real time on partner sites across Europe standing up POCs and showing what our platform can do. You'll also serve as a key technical bridge between our European partners and Rhoda HQ Engineering, owning the feedback loop that turns field findings into product improvements. What You'll Do Scope new partner use cases alongside the commercial team: ask the right questions, assess technical feasibility, and make go/no-go recommendations. Design, prototype, and iterate on end effectors and task-specific tooling for real-world manipulation tasks. Author and refine data collection SOPs, and work with teleoperation and ML ops teams to gather high-quality training data. Post-train and evaluate Rhoda's AI model on partner tasks, driving performance toward POC success criteria. Lead on-site POP/POC setup and execution, including model training, daily reporting, validation, and direct partner interaction, and author the final technical report. Partner with Solution Engineers on task engineering and solution design input as engagements move toward production. Review proposals and provide technical feedback ahead of purchase orders. Support model training through Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), deployment, and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT). Lead root cause analysis for issues surfaced during deployments, troubleshooting across hardware, firmware, and software until the real cause is found. Share field learnings with product and engineering in Silicon Valley, translating partner-reported issues into prioritized, actionable input for the roadmap. Present clear, non-technical summaries of technical outcomes to partner leadership, and work with the commercial team to tie them to commercial milestones. What You'll Bring BS or MS in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, Computer Science, or a related field. 3–8 years of hands-on experience in robotics, automation, systems integration, or applied engineering in an industrial setting, including real-world deployments or field installations. Strong mechanical design skills, including CAD (e.g., SolidWorks, Onshape, Fusion) and rapid prototyping (3D printing, machining, off-the-shelf components). Working knowledge of machine learning workflows — data collection, training, and evaluation — and comfort working in Python. Experience with robot arms, grippers, and sensors (cameras, depth sensors, LiDAR, IMUs) in real environments, including integration and calibration. Proven track record conducting root cause analysis on complex systems spanning hardware, firmware, and software. Strong problem-solving skills and comfort working with ambiguity in high-stakes environments. Clear communicator who can explain technical tradeoffs to partners, executives, and internal teams. Fluent English required; German at working level minimum. Willingness to travel approximately 40% across Europe, including extended on-site POC periods, with occasional travel to the US. Nice to Have Experience with imitation learning, VLA models, world models, or robot foundation models. Background in factory automation, material handling, or logistics. Experience in a customer-facing technical role (application, field, FDE, or sales engineering) at a robotics OEM, system integrator, or corporate automation department. Familiarity with teleoperation systems or remote robot management workflows. Experience with ROS/ROS2, embedded Linux, or C/Rust for onboard software. Why Rhoda AI GmbH Work on real customer problems, not lab demos: our robots are ready for field deployment directly after a successful POC. Direct line to HQ Engineering — your field intelligence shapes the product roadmap. Small, high-ownership team where you work with the Managing Director and Commercial Lead as peers from day one. We are a small team moving fast, and the right person is as comfortable writing a port map, tracing a bad optic, or tuning congestion control on the data center floor as they are setting technical direction.

  • Own the fabric architecture for every site: GPU backend fabric (InfiniBand and/or RoCEv2), and GPU frontend Fabric

  • Tune for real workload performance: congestion control, PFC/ECN, adaptive routing, and NCCL settings for both inference and training traffic

  • Debug fabric problems wherever they show up, from a flapping link to a job that’s mysteriously slow

  • Evaluate and select AI Fabric vendors and hardware, and push back with data when something doesn’t meet spec

  • Collaborate across automation and software to help build network monitoring, telemetry, and automation that let a small team run a large fleet, and be the top escalation point for AI Fabric incidents

  • Experience with NVLink / NVL72-class rack-scale systems and how they change scale-out fabric design

  • Experience with GPUDirect RDMA and GPUDirect Storage networks
